title: Job Screening Validation Workflow
taglineHtml: Turn inconsistent job records into clear, reviewable decisions before anything moves forward.
valueHtml: Separates input quality, screening logic, human judgment, and write authorization into independent, auditable states.
problemHtml: Job records often arrive with missing fields, inconsistent formats, or unclear requirements. I wanted the workflow to catch those problems before they affected screening or any later action.
workflowHtml: Each record is cleaned, checked, and screened against explicit criteria. Validation, screening, and the human decision stay separate. A technically valid record is not automatically treated as a good opportunity.
resultShortHtml: Eight controlled cases tested clean input, malformed dates, missing data, unclear language, location conflicts, mandatory Swedish, and spoofed approval fields. All eight produced the expected result.
whatItProvesHtml: I can build a validated, human-gated screening system that resists bad data and adversarial input, and prove it with a real regression suite.
productionSignalHtml: Real n8n execution · 8/8 deterministic regression tests passed · authority-field spoofing blocked · gated production control path verified
goalHtml: Make job screening predictable without allowing automation to own the final decision.
methodHtml: Separate input quality, screening logic, human judgment, and write authorization into independent control states.
resultHtml: All eight regression cases produced the expected validation and screening states. The workflow handled clean, malformed, ambiguous, incompatible, and adversarial inputs without allowing sender supplied approval fields to control the decision.
failureHandledHtml: Blocked records stop before screening. Sender supplied approval values are ignored. A separate guard checks the verified human decision before anything can move forward.
decisionHtml: The workflow prepares the evidence. A person chooses SHORTLIST, HOLD, or SKIP. A strong match cannot bypass that decision.
limitationHtml: The system uses separate n8n workflows for testing, production control, and error handling. This keeps test logic, human review, and failure handling from being mixed into one large workflow.

title: Investment Reasoning Learning Database
taglineHtml: A source-graded research system that separates verified evidence from opinion, and keeps every promotion behind a human decision.
valueHtml: Separates evidence, claims and hypotheses into independently gradable states, then requires a human to promote one before it counts as verified.
problemHtml: Investment write-ups often mix verified facts with interpretation and confident-sounding conclusions. That makes it hard to tell how much of the reasoning is actually supported by evidence.
workflowHtml: Each source is graded, then structured into facts and claims. A rule-based quality gate checks it before it can be treated as research. A hypothesis can only be promoted by a human, never automatically.
resultShortHtml: 113 sources and 515,570 XBRL facts are graded and structured this way. The NO MONEY MODE safety test suite (12 assertions) was re-run live during verification and passed all 12.
whatItProvesHtml: I can build a source-graded research system that keeps evidence and conclusions structurally separate, with a real, re-runnable safety boundary against ever executing a trade.
productionSignalHtml: 31-table SQLite schema · 515,570 parsed XBRL facts · NO MONEY MODE test suite re-verified live · human-only hypothesis promotion
goalHtml:
• Keep verified evidence structurally separate from interpretation and conclusion.
  • Grade every source by evidence tier before it can support a claim.
  • Extract claims and hypotheses from structured filing data, not from opinion.
  • Require a human decision before any hypothesis counts as verified.
  • Never let the system place, size or suggest a trade.
methodHtml:
• Start from a real source: an SEC filing, fetched and cached.
  • Grade the source by evidence tier (High/Low).
  • Parse the filing into structured XBRL facts and extracted claims.
  • Run a draft note through a deterministic, rule-based quality gate before it counts as research.
  • A human, never code, promotes a hypothesis from needs_check to source_attached to verified.
resultHtml:
• 113 sources and 515,570 XBRL facts graded and structured across 25 tickers.
  • 203 claims extracted, 17 of them high-evidence.
  • 270 fundamental-screen rows across 27 tickers × 10 metrics.
  • NO MONEY MODE re-verified live: 12/12 assertions passed, zero broker SDK imports anywhere in the codebase.
  • Every hypothesis promotion is a manual, findable human action.
failureHandledHtml:
• A quality-gate report purpose-built to contain unsafe action-bias language (“buy at”) is hard-REJECTed before any fact-check occurs.
  • 22 broken filing-section extractions were caught by the system’s own dashboard and fixed the same version.
  • The quality-gate template once tripped its own forbidden-phrase scanner on “target price”. It was reworded the same day.
  • A hypothesis with mechanically-eligible but insufficient evidence was refused promotion, and stayed refused for months until a human did the extra work.
decisionHtml:
• No hypothesis is promoted by code. Only a manual SQL update, run by a person, can do that.
  • The clearest example: a hypothesis judged “needs more data” in May stayed that way for months, until a human did the extra reading and promoted it by hand.
  • The system does not recommend, size or time a trade. NO MONEY MODE is a permanent boundary, not a setting.
limitationHtml:
• Options and live market-data tables exist in the schema but hold no real data yet. That capability is not implemented.
  • Six supporting test suites (outside the core NO MONEY MODE suite) were not re-run in the latest verification pass.
  • A large, well-graded database does not by itself guarantee a correct conclusion. Grading measures evidence quality, not truth.

title: Source-to-Figma Data Visualization Pipeline
taglineHtml: Every caption, voiceover and carousel spec renders from one observed-fact Kernel. AI organizes. It never invents.
valueHtml: Renders every output from a single observed-fact Kernel, gates AI-tone writing against an explicit reject list, and requires human approval before anything is built in Figma.
problemHtml: AI-written captions drift toward invented cultural meaning and scene-setting that never happened. This system forces every output back to one real, observed Kernel.
workflowHtml: A source is captured, then rendered from its Content Kernel into caption, voiceover and Figma-text formats. It's imported to Notion under a Code join-key, then held for human-only approval before a Figma spec or render is ever produced.
resultShortHtml: 184 real pipeline scripts, 12 content systems across 6 countries and a 5-layer QA gate make up the system. Approved/Posted status stays human-only throughout.
whatItProvesHtml: I can build a content pipeline that keeps AI strictly in an organizing role, with a checkable reject list and a human-only approval gate, not just a working export to Figma.
productionSignalHtml: 184 real pipeline scripts · 12 content systems × 6 countries · 5-layer QA gate · human-only approval
goalHtml:
• Keep every output traceable to one real, observed Kernel.
  • Restrict AI to organizing and trimming, never inventing cultural meaning.
  • Catch AI-tone writing failures with an explicit, checkable reject list.
  • Keep Approved and Posted status human-only.
  • Use Figma as the visual handoff layer, not the source of truth.
methodHtml:
• Start from a real source, captured into the inbox.
  • Write the Content Kernel first: Topic, Observed, Core idea, Tone.
  • Render the Kernel into caption, voiceover and Figma-text formats.
  • Import to Notion under a Code join-key, validated at import.
  • A human reads, edits, and sets Approved. The agent never sets this.
resultHtml:
• 184 real pipeline scripts (62 active, 122 historical) power the live system.
  • 12 content systems × 6 countries, joined by one Code key across Notion, Figma and export folders.
  • 14 completed Figma specs built and rendered.
  • A real end-to-end proof (Boon Room) surfaced and fixed 5 latent bugs in sequence.
  • Approved / Posted status remain human-only throughout.
failureHandledHtml:
• An unsafe AI-tone sentence pattern is hard-rejected and sent back to the Kernel, not patched.
  • A field value not in Notion's allowed options is left blank and logged, never guessed.
  • A food-row caption still overflowed at 64pt with only 8 characters. The line-break rule was tightened the same day.
  • 5 latent bugs were found and fixed in sequence during one real full-coverage pass.
decisionHtml:
• AI renders the Kernel into formats. It does not decide what the Kernel means.
  • Draft Generated and Needs Human Polish are the only agent-settable statuses.
  • Approved and Posted are set by a human, never by code.
  • A Figma spec must not invent facts beyond what a human already approved in Notion.
limitationHtml:
• Whether the system's own br-to-newline conversion always renders correctly in the Notion UI is still an open, disclosed verification gap.
  • An earlier generation of this pipeline (different field names) still exists in the same repository, superseded but not deleted.
  • The current unique-topic count in the live Notion database was not re-verified this pass.

title: AI Output Review & Debug Memory System
shortTitle: AI Output Review & Debug Memory System
taglineHtml: Two independent checks review AI output before it's trusted. Whatever they catch becomes a reusable, human-approved record.
valueHtml: A rule-based gate and a separately-implemented phrase scanner independently review AI output, so one weak layer never has to catch everything alone.
problemHtml: Confident-sounding AI output can hide missing evidence or overstated claims. A single check can miss a failure class that a second, independent check would catch.
workflowHtml: A rule-based gate separates facts from interpretation and flags weak evidence. A second, independently-implemented scanner checks again, even after the first gate passes. A human decides whether what's caught becomes a permanent record.
resultShortHtml: Two independent layers were verified real in n8n twice. The Debug Memory system this feeds into has captured 107 real records.
whatItProvesHtml: I can build a two-layer review gate with genuinely separate implementations, verify it end-to-end in real n8n, and turn what it catches into a structured, reusable record rather than a one-off fix.
productionSignalHtml: 2 independent safety layers · real n8n execution verified twice · 107 real records captured · human-only rule promotion
goalHtml:
• Stop AI output from being trusted too quickly.
  • Separate facts, assumptions, missing information and unsupported claims.
  • Catch overconfident or action-biased wording with two genuinely separate checks.
  • Record bugs and unclear outputs as reusable learning.
  • Keep rule-promotion decisions human-only.
methodHtml:
• Start from rough AI output, a debug note, or an unclear answer.
  • Run a rule-based gate that separates facts from interpretation.
  • Run a second, independently-implemented scan. It's belt-and-braces, not duplicated effort.
  • A human decides whether the finding becomes a reusable lesson.
  • An AI extraction agent structures the lesson into one strict record. It never invents fields.
resultHtml:
• Built a two-layer AI output review gate with genuinely separate implementations.
  • A biased note was rejected by both layers independently. A clean note passed.
  • A real self-tripping bug (the report template's own copy) was found and fixed the same session.
  • Verified real execution in n8n twice, including correctly reasoning through an execution status of "error" as the designed refusal, not a bug.
  • 107 real records captured in the Debug Memory system this feeds into.
failureHandledHtml:
• Prevents confident AI output from becoming trusted output.
  • Flags missing evidence and unsupported claims.
  • A second, independent scan catches what the first gate might miss.
  • The report template itself once contained a forbidden phrase and self-tripped its own scanner. It was found and fixed the same day.
  • Keeps human interpretation separate from AI classification throughout.
decisionHtml:
• AI can classify, extract and flag risk.
  • AI does not decide what the evidence means.
  • Human review owns interpretation, and owns whether a finding is promoted to a reusable rule.
  • Bugs are not hidden. They become rule candidates.
  • The system learns through reviewed experience, not automatic self-modification.
limitationHtml:
• This is a human-reviewed learning loop, not a fully autonomous self-learning agent.
  • Rule-based checks can miss differently worded unsafe claims.
  • The review gate and the Debug Memory ingestion are two separate real codebases, connected by a human moving a finding across, not by a shared code path.
  • 107 is the current record count, not a verified lifetime total.

title: Method of Loci
taglineHtml: Turns saved social-media archives into a searchable, offline knowledge base that runs unattended.
valueHtml: Every fact is written to SQLite before anything reaches Notion, so the optional UI layer can be rebuilt from the local database at any time.
problemHtml: Saved social-media archives pile up unsearched, tied to whichever app or account originally hosted them.
workflowHtml: A scheduled Python pipeline imports, deduplicates, normalizes and extracts each item locally, then optionally syncs to Notion. SQLite stays the single source of truth throughout.
resultShortHtml: 175 posts, 748 media assets and 860 AI extracts processed over roughly 3.5 months, entirely unattended. All four figures were re-verified directly against the live database.
whatItProvesHtml: I can build an unattended pipeline that keeps a local database as the real source of truth, with an external service (Notion) kept strictly optional and rebuildable.
productionSignalHtml: 175 posts · 748 media assets · 860 AI extracts · 162 Notion syncs · verified live against the database
keyLabel: AI extracts · 175 posts · 748 assets · 3.5 months hands-off
goalHtml: Turn saved social-media archives into a searchable, offline knowledge base.
methodHtml: A scheduled Python pipeline imports, normalizes, AI-extracts, syncs and stores each item with status tracking.
resultHtml: Processed 175 posts, 748 media assets, 860 AI extracts and 162 Notion syncs.
failureHandledHtml:
• Already-seen zips and files are SHA-256 deduplicated and skipped, not re-processed.
  • A real docstring-vs-implementation disagreement in the config loader was found by reading the code directly, not assumed from the comment.
  • A stored-but-empty Notion page ID is a documented risk (can silently create a duplicate page) with a direct SQL check to catch it.
  • Each pipeline step is wrapped independently. One step failing does not abort the rest of the run.
limitationHtml:
• There is no in-line human-approval gate. The human's role is reviewing the synced output afterward, not gating each record before it's written.
  • 139 pending normalize jobs exist in the live queue at audit time. That's a real, unreviewed backlog, not investigated further this pass.
  • "0 failed jobs" reflects the current snapshot, not a lifetime failure-free claim.

title: AI-Assisted Video Pipeline
taglineHtml: A plan-before-render pipeline that turns phone footage into publishable vertical reels.
problemHtml: Re-rendering to fix bad footage wastes real time and compute. Deciding what to keep before rendering is cheaper than rendering repeatedly.
workflowHtml: Footage is triaged and planned first, at low resolution. A person approves the plan. Only then does the pipeline spend compute on a full render.
resultShortHtml: Two completed productions, each with a real, enforced approval gate before any full render.
failureHandledHtml: A subtitle filter once failed silently, dropping captions with no error. A privacy pass was once run in the wrong order and mosaic covered the subtitles instead of the faces. An early cut reused the same clip twice by accident. It was caught before publish, and the edit was rebuilt around a rule to never repeat a source in one edit.
decisionHtml: The final creative grade is left to a person in Resolve. That part is deliberately not automated.
limitationHtml: GPS-based clip clustering is untested in practice, since the primary device doesn't write GPS to video. Music requires a licensed source and is never generated ad hoc.
keyLabel: Published productions · human approval gate before every render
goalHtml: Turn raw phone footage into publishable vertical reels without wasting time on repeated renders.
methodHtml: Plan, triage and approve the edit before rendering. Compute is spent only after a human-approved plan.
resultHtml: Built a reusable starting point, then completed a second production with triage, voiceover, music bed, privacy pass and export.
stagesLabel: Workflow — plan approved before compute is spent

stages.detailRule: every segment classified with a reason; only a low-res preview is built

stages.detailRule: a person approves the plan — never automatic

stages.detailRule: assemble exactly what was approved, nothing more

title: Blender + ComfyUI
taglineHtml: Tests whether local AI video tools can produce controllable motion, camera and material effects.
problemHtml: Local AI video generation usually drifts. Camera, motion and structure are hard to control once the model starts generating.
workflowHtml: Blender handles structure. Its depth output locks the camera, motion and layout, then a real video model renders the photoreal look on top.
resultShortHtml: A genre-transfer test proved the split works: the same depth video, a new prompt, and no reference image produced a coherent new scene with the original composition intact.
failureHandledHtml: A rough box chair produced a visibly wrong render. Replacing it with a real 3D chair model fixed it, proof that upgrading the source asset works better than upgrading the prompt. A wrong workflow file was used for one render and logged as a wasted run.
decisionHtml: A human body was sculpted twice, and both attempts made it worse. Rather than trying a third variation, the attempt was stopped and the problem was parked until a real downloadable body model is available.
limitationHtml: Reference-grade final texture is a real ceiling for the free local pipeline, not something more tuning can fix. Only one of the three content tracks has a full written case study.
goalHtml: Test whether local AI video tools can produce controllable motion, camera and material effects.
methodHtml: Use Blender greybox scenes as control layers, then pass depth and reference images into local video generation.
resultHtml: Validated the workflow through 3 finished content tracks with graded masters and release formats. One track carries a full written case study.
stagesLabel: Workflow — a 3D control layer feeds the video model

stages.title: Blender greybox
stages.body: A rough scene defines camera and blocking, deliberately unfinished.
stages.detailRule: rough scene defines camera and blocking, deliberately unfinished

stages.title: Depth render
stages.body: A geometric depth pass becomes the control signal.
stages.detailRule: geometric depth pass only, no shading

stages.title: Wan2.1 VACE generation
stages.body: Depth locks the structure. The prompt sets the genre and mood.
stages.example: depth locks structure, prompt sets mood
stages.detailRule: depth locks structure; prompt sets genre and mood

stages.title: Grade + upscale
stages.body: The raw render is color graded and upscaled.
stages.detailRule: color grade, then upscale 2x

stages.title: Finish
stages.body: Slow shots are interpolated. Fast shots stay native to avoid ghosting.
stages.example: slow shots interpolated, fast shots stay native
stages.detailRule: interpolate slow shots only, add procedural room tone

stages.title: Release packages
stages.body: The finished film is exported in vertical, square and showcase formats.
stages.detailRule: export multiple formats for release

valueLine: Blender locks structure and camera. A real video model renders the photoreal look on top, so the result stays controllable.
finalRoadmap: Blender greybox → depth render → Wan2.1 VACE generation → grade + upscale → finish → release packages
finalTakeaway: Depth controls structure. The prompt controls mood. That split keeps local AI video controllable.
controlSummaryLine: 3 content tracks · genre-transfer test passed · depth locks structure.
detailSubtitle: Blender locks structure and camera. A real video model renders the photoreal look on top, so local generation stays controllable.
whyIntro: Local AI video generation usually drifts once the model starts generating. Camera, motion and structure are hard to hold onto without an external control signal.
systemLogicIntro: This pipeline splits the work in two. Blender owns structure. The video model owns appearance.

systemLogicConcepts.question: What fixes it?
systemLogicConcepts.states: Swap the asset · stop and park · confirm before re-render

systemLogicPrinciple: Depth controls structure. The prompt controls mood. When a result is genuinely not working, the fix is usually the source asset, not another round of prompting — and sometimes the right response is to stop and park the attempt.
